audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart on both layers (Skill/Illaoi/Illaoi/Skill/Skill/Illaoi/Illaoi) contradicts the packet chart (Darius/Darius/Darius/Skill/Illaoi/Skill/Skill), the whys[] text (which already says Darius owns 1-3 and Illaoi flips at 6), and the already-audited mirror darius__illaoi, which set both layers to the packet shape.
audit.why: Illaoi has no early trading pattern before Test of Spirit is up and safe to cast; Darius's Decimate blade edge heals him and Crippling Strike slows for free autos. Level 6 is her window because Leap of Faith spawns a tentacle per champion hit. First item and late are execution-dependent both ways.
audit.corrected: Level chart set to the packet/mirror shape on both layers as one atomic group, with phases[0/1/2/4/5/6].why rewritten so no row's prose argues against its side. Ratings left alone — polarity is ambiguous and the mirror did not touch them either.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[2].why and phases[5].why claimed Illaoi spikes without naming a real cooldown, and phases[6].why asserted a side-lane win the chart no longer supports.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s — it is the timer the whole lane is played around, and quoting the rank-3 value (21s) makes the level-3 advice concrete. Leap of Faith is 120/95/70s and spawns one tentacle per champion hit.
audit.corrected: Level 3 why now names Apprehend at 21s at rank 3 plus Decimate resets; level 6 why names the tentacle-per-champion spawn; first item framed as the Iceborn Gauntlet slow versus his pull; two items framed as a coinflip on Test of Spirit.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1].d ('Get pulled into a 5-stack') carried unrelated filler about burning a cooldown, and dontsFull[2].d ('Trade into his outer Q') never said what the outer Q actually does. report[5].t, the Key Ability Interactions block, gave no cooldown number.
audit.why: Riot's Decimate text: enemies struck by the blade (the outer ring) take more damage than those struck by the handle, and Darius heals off champions hit by the blade. Hemorrhage stacks to 5 and enrages him for massive AD at max stacks, and Noxian Guillotine's true damage scales per stack — so being pulled to five stacks is what feeds his R, and his R's true damage means stacking armour is the wrong answer.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d now states Apprehend into five Hemorrhage stacks enrages him and feeds R; dontsFull[2].d states the blade edge carries the damage and the heal, so stand at handle range; report[5].t now carries Apprehend's real 26s/16s rank-1/rank-5 cooldowns and the bait-then-E-W sequence.

audit.why: report[8].t already calls Executioner's Calling early against his Decimate healing, which satisfies the needs-antiheal missing-interaction rule.

edits.before: Plant tentacles before contesting anything. Identify how Darius contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Darius owns level 1: his Q blade edge heals off you. Plant tentacles on terrain and concede the first wave, not a trade.

edits.before: Landing E changes the lane — his soul fuels your field. Only take the trade when Darius's Apprehend is down.
edits.after: Level 2 is his: Crippling Strike slows you for free autos. Take Test of Spirit only when Apprehend is down.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Darius must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but Apprehend (21s at rank 3) plus Decimate resets still beat you. Keep the wave near your terrain and farm.

edits.before: Leap of Faith inside your tentacle field is a 1v3 button. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Darius's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Level 6 is yours: Leap of Faith spawns a tentacle per champion hit, and the swarm out-damages his Guillotine reset attempt.

edits.before: Iceborn Gauntlet is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Apprehend's cooldown.
edits.after: First item is a skill check: Iceborn Gauntlet's slow lands tentacles, his Apprehend undoes it.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Darius carry threat 9/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on, it stays a coinflip: your swarm wins the long fight, one missed Test of Spirit hands him the Guillotine reset.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Apprehend into five Hemorrhage stacks enrages him and feeds R.

edits.before: Fighting in open ground with no tentacles — Illaoi without her field is the weakest juggernaut in the game.
edits.after: Decimate's blade edge does the big damage and heals him off you — stand at the handle range or step out.

edits.before: Track Darius's Apprehend (Pull): His all-in starts on the pull. Don’t get caught. When it is down — Slam him in your field.
edits.after: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — his all-in starts on that pull. Bait it, then Test of Spirit and W into your tentacles.

notes: Chart flips proposed as one matched group across both layers (6 rows; phases[3]/win[3] already agree at Skill). Ratings untouched, matching the mirror. FLAG MISFIRE confirmed from the mirror and re-checked here: Illaoi's R carries derived flags 'grounding' and 'untargetable' but Riot's text says only that she smashes her idol into the ground, damages nearby enemies, and spawns a tentacle per champion hit — the flags almost certainly fired on the phrase 'into the ground'. Neither is asserted anywhere in these edits. Darius's R deals true damage, so the resistances-invalidated rule means armour stacking is not the answer; I did not add that to itemization text because report[8] is already at its length band and the anti-heal line there is the higher-value fact.
